target: A no-wait decontamination station receives vehicles as a Poisson process at 5 per hour. Each occupied bay has exponential service time with mean 2 hours. If every bay is occupied, an arriving vehicle is diverted immediately and never queues. The station requires the long-run diversion probability to be below 1%. The team must choose the smallest integer number of identical bays under this loss-system model.
surface: A previous field-service plan provisioned from average concurrency. It multiplied 5 arrivals/hour by 2 service-hours to get 10 occupied bays on average, added 20% headroom, and selected 12 bays without calculating a diversion probability.
structural: A telephone trunk group with Poisson calls, exponential holding times, c circuits, and no waiting used Erlang B. With offered load A=lambda/mu, it evaluated B(0,A)=1 and recursively B(c,A)=A*B(c-1,A)/(c+A*B(c-1,A)), choosing the first integer c whose blocking probability fell below the target.
rubric: Explicitly selects the M/M/c/c Erlang-B loss formula rather than average concurrency or Erlang C.
Computes offered load A=5*2=10 Erlangs and uses the Erlang-B recursion.
Computes B(17,10) about 0.01295 and B(18,10) about 0.00714.
Chooses 18 bays as the smallest count below 1% diversion.
States reliance on Poisson arrivals, exponential holding, independent offered traffic, and no waiting.
